sourceNote: The T-pose polar bear mesh of the user, of 2026-10-24 (assets/models/polar-bear/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist. The user said: "now apply similar techniques to the polars bear", after the quad arms of the Rigify rabbit. tools/blender/polar_bear_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. The faces of the paws, the trunk, the legs, and the head are the faces of the user.
paintedNote: The weights of the trunk, the head, and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/polar_bear_arms.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower (the hips, the trunk up to the chest, the legs, and the tail) keep the rule weights. Blender weights on the legs sank the tail into the haunch and folded faces on the bench (branch rigify-polar-bear). Blender weights on spine and spine1 folded a V of faces on the lower back over the bench, and on the chest they cut a slit into the side of the trunk under each arm in the play.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the three rings of its joint in the bind. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts). They replace upperTwist.

name: Polar Bear

app.note: 0.85 of the size of the studio polar bear before the meshes (the skull top at 1.923 m), because the user said that the bear was too tall (docs/decisions/2026-10-24-polar-bear-seat.md). The skull top of the mesh is at 1.0 u, so the scale is 1.63455 m for each unit. The leg factor raises the standing shoulder joints from 0.725 u, and the landmark rises with them, so that the trunk, the head, and the arms keep their meters. The reach is the reach of the arm factor below.

armFactorNote: The arms keep the length of the mesh (user rule: keep the limbs of a mesh of the user, and fit the props).
legFactorNote: The user chose longer legs with the size kept for the polar bear mesh on 2026-10-22 ("Longer legs, keep size"), because with short legs the round belly hid the lap on the bench, and the seated bear read almost as standing (docs/research/2026-10-22-polar-legs.md). The T-pose mesh has short legs too, so it keeps the factor 1.6.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the skull top, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-24-polar-bear-tpose/. The legs part below the crotch at y 0.20. The thigh joint lies inside the haunch at y 0.28, as on the polar bear mesh of 2026-10-22, the knee at y 0.15, and the ankle at the narrowest leg cut. With the thigh joint at the crotch, the thigh was too short to sit level, and the seat rule pulled the rump down 44 cm. The neck is narrowest at y 0.63, and the head starts at y 0.79. The arms are in a T-pose: each round arm goes out level at y 0.73, free of the trunk beyond x 0.145 (sections-x.txt). The cuts across the arm axis give its middle line (arm-axis.txt): the shoulder joint lies inside the root of the arm, the elbow at x 0.29, the wrist where the paw starts (x 0.435), and the forearm twist halfway between them. The finger joint lies at the root of the claws. The ears start at y 0.96, and a ball tail sits at y 0.26 to 0.33 behind the rump. In the T-pose, the palm faces down.

studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it: the thighs 5 degrees down and 15 degrees out, and the shins vertical, so that the knee angle from the side is 95 degrees, as a real pianist sits with the thighs level or a little down to the knees (leg_turns.py of docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open/ 5 15 0). With the thighs 30 degrees out, the knees did not show more from the camera of the stage, and the rest folded more faces. The trunk shares and the bind arms are the values of the other meshes. A forward lean of the bind (open -12 or -18) folded both arms in each play sample, so the trunk keeps the seat of the source, and the play lean of the hold leans the spine (docs/research/2026-10-22-polar-seat.md).

armFree.note: The arm of the T-pose is free of the trunk beyond x 0.145, from y 0.65 to 0.79, and the trunk there ends below y 0.53 (sections-x.txt). A vertex of the free arm lies beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, within radius of the chain of the arm joints, and above the floor.

line.note: The angle of the other meshes of 2026-10-23: a lower angle mixes the weights of long arm faces.

knee.note: Each vertex splits its weight of the thigh and the shin by its height: the thigh share grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, around the knee joint at 0.15. Bone heat on the short thick legs gave the shin the front of the knee and the underside of the thigh up to the haunch, and these vertices stayed upright with the shin when the seated thigh turned forward: the knee stood as a hump above the thigh (user, 2026-10-26: "the polar bear's knee is unexpectedly bulky"). The bands 0.13 to 0.18 and 0.14 to 0.17 gave the same form with a harder crease at the knee. The slab from the heel to the haunch stayed with each band, because long faces cross the knee: the rings of refine cut them.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the rump stays on the bench and the thigh turns forward. With the ramp of 0.17 to 0.28, the hips held most of the thigh, and the seated thigh bent only near the knee. With this ramp, the thigh turns as one tube from the haunch to the knee, and the bench is 2.7 cm lower.

weights.note: Beyond the plane of armSplit (armFree), only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only. armTop starts above the top of the level arms of the T-pose (y 0.79): from y 0.68, it gave the top of each arm to the neck, and those faces folded in each sample. Each ear follows its ear bone above earBase. The short tail is a ball on one bone (tailBall). The rig has no cut and no split of the arms (user, 2026-10-23). Rings of new vertices cut the long faces of the knees (refine.rings, user, 2026-10-26).

refine.ringsNote: The source leg has faces that run from near the crotch to the ankle across the knee joint (35 faces on each leg, a longest edge of 0.185 units on the median). A face cannot bend, so in the seated bind it stayed one flat plane from the thigh to the shin: the knee read as a large angular block with hard ridges, and long faces from the calf to the haunch made a slab under the thigh (user, 2026-10-26: "the polar bear's knees are more bulky than it should be"). The weight bands of the knee and the haunch, and a seat with the thighs or the shins 10 degrees down, kept the slab. Rings of new vertices cut these faces, and each new vertex takes the knee and haunch rules at its height (ring_leg_weights() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Three rings cut the front half of each knee (toward +z, within 90 degrees): at the knee plane, 0.05 units above it, and 0.04 units below it. Two rings cut the back half: 0.1 units above the knee plane and 0.08 units below it. The bent knee puts each back vertex nearer to the knee plane than the radius of the leg inside the leg, so whole rings at the back folded the skin into stacked light stripes under the thigh. The back rings stand where the thigh and the shin meet in the bind, so their vertices stay on the skin. With a radius of 0.17, the slab under the thigh stayed. With the front rings 0.04 above and below, one face between the thighs folded in each play sample. A cut keeps 0.2 of the edge at each end: with 0.1, two thin faces of the inner right thigh folded in the play.

flip.note: The values of the other meshes.

check.note: The values of the other meshes.

shift.note: The fur of the mesh is cream: Oklab lightness 0.896 and b 0.042 (dark-faces.txt), against the white of polar-bear-views.png and SPECIES_COLORS of the polar bear (#efeae0). As the panda rule asks, each fur face with a chroma from 0.01 to 0.02 and up, and a lightness above 0.5 to 0.6, takes 1.045 of its lightness and 0.3 of its chroma. The black nose, eyes, and claws keep their colors.

colors.note: The color shift of the polar bear mesh of 2026-10-22 moves the cream fur toward the white of the reference. With the dark limit 0.0037 of that mesh, 12.1% of the faces outside the eye and nose boxes were dark, and with 0.0015 none.

eyeShell.note: The values of the other meshes.

chair.note: The seat is the piano bench of the pianist (prop): it is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The front edge lies under the hip joints, where the thighs leave the haunch, and the back edge at the back of the haunch. The half width holds the haunch (x ±0.23). PIANO_BENCH of src/models/instruments/piano.ts takes this width and depth in meters.

crease.note: The values of the other meshes.

kneeCrease.note: The faces at the corner of each bent knee turned more than the crease angle of the app (40 degrees) from each other, so each showed as a light wedge at the back of the knee. The seam is each vertex of both a thigh face and a shin face on the inner side of the knee. It and two rings of its neighbors move half of the way to the middle of their neighbors in each of 4 rounds (knee_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). With 1 ring and 3 rounds, a thin light line stayed on the calf from behind and the right.

sit.note: The values of the dog and the deer.
